text: • For this exercise, we used high data center load, regional projections from EER (Jones et al. 2024), which are on a 5-year timescale (2030, 2035, …, 2050). ◦ We used an 88% utilization factor to convert from projected load to capacity. ◦ Initial (2025) locations come from Baxtel1 dataset. – Initial data center capacity linearly scaled to match that of the EER 2025 values so that 2050 deployment levels are aligned. • Grid cells are characterized and normalized to a 5.76-km x 5.76-km resolution. *Only showing projections for regions with more than 500 MW of load by 2050. 1 U.S. Data Center Sites. Downscaling Results Downscaling Results • Site suitability scores are obtained from the random forest feature importance scores. • Feature importance values are normalized such that the total is equal to 1. This is then plugged into the site suitability module to produce site suitability scores. • With the site suitability scores from the random forest approach, reVeal predicts the location and size of data centers through 2050. ◦ We limit growth to a maximum 1 GW per site per time-step to account for construction times as well as distribute load across all sites. *Only shows sites with more than 50 MW National Laboratory of the Rockies | 24 Case Study: Lesson Learned and Limitations Case Study: Lesson Learned and Limitations • Our current approach tends to cluster sites around population centers because of a lack of spatially explicit data for several important variables: ◦ Local transmission hosting capacity ◦ Local demand queue times ◦ Local zoning, ordinance, and permitting information ◦ Social acceptance ◦ Varying suitability considerations for different data center types. • Similarly, our site suitability model leverages historical data center buildout patterns to predict future development, though these patterns may not fully reflect emerging trends. • Ongoing work is assessing the above considerations and will be integrated into reVeal when available. National Laboratory of the Rockies | 25 Conclusions Conclusions • By integrating results into ReEDS, reVeal enables highly resolved spatiotemporal data center load forecasts that are not otherwise available for advanced power systems modeling. • Additional information such as transmission hosting capacity and load interconnection queue considerations will improve the fidelity of reVeal downscaling results.
